gen_risks.description: Integrating FOAK carbon capture technology at an operational cement plant at scale introduces potential technical integration and performance risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct independent technical assurance via third-party experts and enforce strict performance thresholds within the Industrial Carbon Capture contract.
gen_risks.evidence: Padeswood will be the first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology

gen_risks.description: Spurline development delays could force a 4-month delay to Final Investment Decision (FID) and a 5-month delay to Commercial Operation Date (COD).
gen_risks.mitigation: Proactively align spurline delivery timelines and project FID milestones via the Cluster Sponsor Function oversight body.
gen_risks.evidence: FID is delayed by 4 months to align with their spurline timelines, resulting in a subsequent 5-month delay to COD

gen_risks.description: Rising carbon prices and exposure to unabated overseas competition risk carbon leakage and loss of market share prior to full CCUS operation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Industrial Carbon Capture revenue support contracts to bridge the operating cost gap and maintain market competitiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Without CCUS, the cement industry will increasingly be exposed to a rising carbon price, impacting competitiveness with imports.

gen_risks.description: Internationally owned corporate parent may de-prioritise UK interests and reallocate investment overseas if UK decarbonisation frameworks lag.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long-term policy and commercial certainty through 25-year business model frameworks and Grant Funding Agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Most UK cement sites are operated by companies that are internationally owned and make investment decisions on a global basis.

gen_risks.description: High upfront capital expenditure during capture facility construction creates risk of cost overruns and funding shortfalls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide upfront capital support via the CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant up to 50% of eligible costs using an Open Book Model.
gen_risks.evidence: The CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant, which provides upfront capital support during the construction phase, up to 50% of Padeswood’s eligible capital costs.

gen_risks.description: Interdependent cross-chain interfaces between the Padeswood capture plant and the broader HyNet T&S network create operational delivery risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Cluster Sponsor Function to actively manage cross-chain delivery and operating model integration risks.
gen_risks.evidence: Managing government-owned cross-chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks.

gen_risks.description: Fluctuations in captured CO2 volumes or operational disruptions create income uncertainty under long-term support contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure revenue support under a Contract-for-Difference model tying payments to captured CO2 performance and volume thresholds.
gen_risks.evidence: address key market barriers facing CCS deployment – such as high upfront costs, cross-chain risks, and revenue uncertainty

gen_risks.description: Premature project discontinuation during development or operation could result in major write-downs of public capital and unfulfilled carbon targets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and continuous compliance monitoring by LCCC and DESNZ CGL.

gen_risks.description: Potential fraudulent claims or financial mismanagement in grant drawdowns and revenue support disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement Open Book Model cost assessments, independent financial assurance, and CGL grant compliance oversight.

gen_risks.description: Exchequer financial exposure under Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and Government Support Package variations during remediation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Subject all variation requests and Government Support Package decisions to rigorous review by the Cluster Sponsor Function and SRO.
gen_risks.evidence: 5.4.3 Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA)

gen_risks.description: Underutilisation of the HyNet transport and storage network capacity if captured CO2 volumes fall short of projections.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor unutilised capacity metrics and accelerate competitive selection for build-out users to maximize network utilisation.
gen_risks.evidence: Volume of unutilised network capacity (Mtpa) across the clusters by 2030

gen_risks.description: Implementation of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) in 2027 may expose unabated domestic cement production if capture deployment slips.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align project delivery milestones with 2027 CBAM timelines to ensure domestic decarbonised cement is market-ready.
gen_risks.evidence: The UK Carbon-Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)... will be introduced in 2027. However, unabated UK sites would be competing with sites overseas.

gen_risks.description: Shortages in specialized CCUS supply chain capacity and technical skills could delay construction and upskilling objectives.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor supply chain spend, support regional workforce training, and track skill level metrics over the support contract lifespan.
gen_risks.evidence: Stimulate the CCUS supply chain, jobs, and skills, over the support contracts’ lifespans

gen_risks.description: Operational reliance on external network operator T&SCo (Liverpool Bay) and economic regulation by Ofgem introduces third-party dependency risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require strict adherence to the CCS Network Code and coordinate multi-party oversight through the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function.
gen_risks.evidence: Ofgem: Economic Regulator for T&S Network Users and T&SCo (Liverpool Bay)

gt_risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) risk. RSA would be paid to the T&S Company (Eni) in two circumstances: where the network is underutilised, and where users are unavailable to inject CO2 and therefore are not paying user fees. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.1, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Padeswood joining the T&S network will reduce the level of network underutilisation and will therefore reduce RSA payments to the T&SCo.

gt_risks.description: Discontinuation risk for Padeswood: the potential for Padeswood to be unable to continue under the business model contract due to the actions of another party or events outside its control - a large-scale, programme-wide issue (e.g. leakage), a prolonged T&S issue, or external events such as Qualifying Change in Law (QCiL), Qualifying Shutdown Events, or Force Majeure. Projects connected via a spurline can also be exposed to an additional risk if the spurline FID is taken after T&S FID, which is not within the capture project's control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.2, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The risk of having to make a discontinuation payment to Padeswood is judged to be a remote contingent liability given that it is very unlikely (<1%); spurline-timing risk is treated as a variation of the existing cross-chain risks already protected by the business model.

gt_risks.description: Exchequer funding / Secretary of State direct agreement (SoSDA) risk: LCCC is only liable to make payments to the extent it has received sufficient funds from HMG, creating a risk that Padeswood would have no recourse under its private-law contract with LCCC to obtain payments owed if HMG funding to LCCC were insufficient. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.3, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: The Secretary of State will sign a direct agreement with Padeswood (to which LCCC is also party) to fund payments directly where LCCC fails to pay; this does not increase DESNZ's overall liabilities or create a contingent liability, as it is an intragroup transaction.

gt_risks.description: Fraud risk across the CCUS programme's grant and contract payments. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.4, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: A CCUS Fraud Management Strategy is being developed specifying the programme's strategic approach to deterrence, prevention, detection, and management of fraud and error, including counter-fraud governance and reporting structures and high-quality fraud risk assessments (FRAs) for the different tranches of the CCUS programme.

gt_risks.description: Financial sensitivities: several contractual terms are 'locked in' at Padeswood FID, but drivers of the financial impact continue to move post-FID - notably the carbon market price (Low ETS series used as the reference price for the extension period) and the opex reopener (higher opex expenditure payments), both of which could result in higher subsidy. Other financial sensitivities have the effect of reducing total subsidy. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.5, p.14-15.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to estimate the scale of potential subsidy increase from each driver; offsetting sensitivities are also identified and tracked.

gt_risks.description: Cross-chain and cross-cutting risks. Cross-chain risks are risks the private sector is exposed to through the network but cannot mitigate against - T&S Construction delay, Padeswood Construction Delay, Padeswood Underperformance, T&S Underperformance, and Discontinuation Provisions; Padeswood joining the HyNet cluster increases HMG's exposure to compensation payments should the T&S network fail or become unavailable. Cross-cutting risks - inflation risk, carbon price risk, and OpEx risk - are those which are challenging for the private sector to price or relate to events outside their control. [Financial Case Sec 5.4.6, p.14-15; overlaps in subject matter with the Economic Case's Sec 3.4 Risk Appraisal tables, p.10-11, which quantify the value-for-money impact of the same named risks but are a modelling input rather than a risk-register entry, and are excised from planning text for leakage safety but not scored here.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Risk allocation is designed so that each risk sits with the party best placed to manage it; the business model contracts and Network Code are structured to limit and price cross-chain exposure.
